candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Instream Waste Concentration table column headers
candidates.exact_span:
POLLUTANTS                                             Conc          Conc.       Aquatic      Supply       Aquatic       Health       Criteria   Criteria       Criteria     Criteria    Criteria   Criteria
                                CAS No.       MQL     Ca (ug/l)    Ce (ug/l)     2.13*Ce   Cd,dom (ug/l)   Cd (ug/l)   Cd,hh (ug/l)     ug/l       ug/l          ug/l          ug/l        ug/l       ug/l
candidates.computation_change_reason: The table presents multiple numeric columns (effluent concentration Ce, formula-derived instream concentrations, and separate human-health/aquatic criteria). Which column is treated as the enforceable discharge limit versus a derived background or narrative criterion would change limit selection and exceedance determinations for reported measurements.

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Instream Waste Concentration table, MQL column
candidates.computation_change_reason: MQL values define method quantification limits for each pollutant row. Interpreting whether reported values below MQL are comparable to numeric limits, treated as non-detect, or leave compliance unresolved would change exceedance outcomes (A) and how missing or sub-quantification evidence is classified (C).

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Instream Waste Concentration table, Mercury dissolved row
candidates.computation_change_reason: This row has no Ce value but mixes zeros, finite criteria (1.4; 0.77), and 1E+100 placeholders. Interpreting blank Ce versus zero criteria versus 1E+100 as 'no numeric limit' would change whether an enforceable limit exists for dissolved mercury and whether absent or low results imply compliance, no comparison, or unresolved evidence.

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Instream Waste Concentration table, Mercury total row
candidates.computation_change_reason: Mercury is listed in both dissolved and total forms with different Ce and criteria values. Whether reported mercury measurements must be matched to dissolved, total, or either form would change the applicable limit (A) and which monitoring obligation applies to a given sample (B).

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Instream Waste Concentration table, Nickel dissolved (P) row
candidates.computation_change_reason: The '(P)' designation appears on some dissolved-metal rows but not on corresponding total-recoverable rows. Interpreting '(P)' as provisional, priority, or another permit-specific modifier could change whether this row's Ce and criteria are enforceable limits and whether dissolved-nickel monitoring is required.

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Instream Waste Concentration table, Selenium dissolved (P) row
candidates.computation_change_reason: This row lists dissolved selenium with no Ce but finite criteria, alongside a separate conditional row below. Whether the '(P)' row applies by default, only under certain conditions, or is superseded by the sulfate-conditioned row would change limit selection (A), monitoring applicability (B), and how missing dissolved-selenium results are classified when conditions are undocumented (C).

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Instream Waste Concentration table, Selenium dis (SO4 >500 mg/l) row
candidates.computation_change_reason: This row states a sulfate-conditioned variant of the dissolved selenium criteria (e.g., irrigation criterion 250 vs 130 on the prior row). Interpreting when SO4 > 500 mg/l is met, whether sulfate must be measured to choose the row, and whether monitoring is required only under that condition would change applicable limits (A), conditional monitoring obligations (B), and whether absent selenium data reflects conditional non-requirement or missing evidence (C).

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Instream Waste Concentration table, Selenium total recoverable row
candidates.computation_change_reason: Selenium appears as dissolved (including conditional) and total recoverable with different Ce values (blank/conditional vs 1.5). Matching reported selenium speciation to the correct row would change which numeric limit applies and which monitoring form is obligated.

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Instream Waste Concentration table, 1E+100 placeholder values
candidates.computation_change_reason: Many cells use the sentinel 1E+100 across domestic, irrigation, wildlife, and aquatic criteria columns. Interpreting 1E+100 as no applicable numeric criterion (report-only or non-operative) versus a literal numeric limit would change whether compliance comparisons are performed (A) and whether missing data for that parameter should be treated as outside numeric compliance scope or unresolved (C).

candidates.locator: Page 26, Section: fact_sheet, Instream Waste Concentration table, Need TMDL column
candidates.computation_change_reason: The Need TMDL column is present for every pollutant row and is uniformly marked N/A in this segment. Interpreting whether N/A means no TMDL-based limit applies, TMDL limits are elsewhere, or TMDL status is undetermined would change whether TMDL-derived limits are considered part of applicable discharge limits.
